title: Homogeneous zero relations on a regular sequence
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $f_1,\ldots,f_c$ an $R$-regular sequence [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence], allowing $c=0$. Put $J=(f_1,\ldots,f_c)$ [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient]. Let $p\in R[T_1,\ldots,T_c]$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring] be homogeneous of any total degree $n\geq0$. If $p(f_1,\ldots,f_c)=0$, every coefficient of $p$ belongs to $J$.

source.place: Tag 00LN (lemma-regular-quasi-regular), proof (1), zero-relation induction on the length and largest exponent of the last variable.

proof.text: Expand every element of J^(n+1) as the evaluation of a degree-n homogeneous polynomial all of whose coefficients belong to J: write J^(n+1)=J*J^n and use the homogeneous spanning description of J^n. Subtraction reduces the next-power coefficient assertion to the zero-relation assertion.

source.place: Tag 00LN (lemma-regular-quasi-regular), proof (1), zero-relation induction on the length and largest exponent of the last variable.

proof.text: Induct on sequence length for weakly regular sequences, simultaneously in all degrees, proving the next-power assertion by this subtraction. With no variables every polynomial is constant and J=0, so membership in J^(n+1) forces that constant to vanish. For a nonempty sequence let g be its prefix, K its ideal and t its last generator. Weak regularity gives a weakly regular prefix and injectivity of multiplication by every power of t on R/K.

source.place: Tag 00LN (lemma-regular-quasi-regular), proof (1), zero-relation induction on the length and largest exponent of the last variable.

proof.text: Regard a degree-n homogeneous zero relation as a polynomial in the last variable with prefix-polynomial coefficients a_e homogeneous of degree n-e. Its last-variable degree l is at most n. Induct on l. At l=0 the prefix next-power assertion applies to the zero value and places every coefficient in K, hence in J.

source.place: Tag 00LN (lemma-regular-quasi-regular), proof (1), zero-relation induction on the length and largest exponent of the last variable.

proof.text: At l>0 the lower-exponent evaluated terms lie in K^(n-l+1). Thus t^l times the evaluation of a_l lies there too. The prefix assertion in degree n-l puts t^l times every coefficient of a_l in K. Cancel t^l modulo K to place those coefficients themselves in K.

source.place: Tag 00LN (lemma-regular-quasi-regular), proof (1), zero-relation induction on the length and largest exponent of the last variable.

proof.text: For a homogeneous prefix polynomial of degree d whose coefficients are in K, expand each coefficient in the prefix generators and replace each generator in that coefficient by its variable. The result q is homogeneous of degree d+1 with the same evaluated value. Apply this to a_l; replacing a_(l-1) by a_(l-1)+t*q rewrites the relation with maximal exponent l-1. The inner induction places the modified coefficients in J. Subtract the corrections, which are multiples of t in J. The top coefficients already belong to K. This proves the zero-relation assertion and, by subtraction, the next-power assertion for the longer sequence.

source.place: Tag 00LN (lemma-regular-quasi-regular), proof (1), zero-relation induction on the length and largest exponent of the last variable.

proof.text: Specialize the proved next-power assertion to a regular sequence and to evaluation zero, which belongs to J^(n+1). This proves the displayed zero-relation conclusion in every length and degree.

source.place: Tag 00LN (lemma-regular-quasi-regular), proof (1), zero-relation induction on the length and largest exponent of the last variable.

lean.statement:
theorem regularSequence_homogeneous_relation {R : Type u} [CommRing R]
    {c : ℕ} (f : Fin c → R) (hf : RingTheory.Sequence.IsRegular R (List.ofFn f))
    (n : ℕ) (p : MvPolynomial (Fin c) R) (hp : p.IsHomogeneous n) (hz : p.eval f = 0) :
    ∀ d, p.coeff d ∈ Ideal.span (Set.range f)

mathlib_searches.query: If f is a regular sequence and a homogeneous polynomial evaluates in the next power of the ideal generated by f, every coefficient belongs to that ideal
Coefficients of a homogeneous polynomial vanishing at a weakly regular sequence belong to the ideal generated by the sequence
